signature_moves: The drag-target grid IS the product: Launchpad/Stacks tile-grid metaphor repurposed as file destinations, chunked into 3 labeled sections; ~64pt tiles sized for throwing files at, not clicking
Legacy-skeuomorphic soul in modern chrome: glossy gel destination icons (SFTP Upload) and a glossy 3D app icon retained inside a current Sequoia translucent-vibrancy popover
Grouped-control containers: leading and trailing toolbar clusters each share one continuous rounded translucent background with internal dividers
defects: Low UI contrast (rubric #10) — section separators and grouped-control borders are near-invisible hairlines (<3:1); panel structure leans on the faintest fills over vibrancy

Borderline glass-on-glass (native audit #2) — translucent grouped control pills on translucent panel material; fine in big-sur vibrancy, a Liquid Glass violation if re-skinned for macOS 26+ without solidifying controls
Within-app material inconsistency — modern translucent chrome vs glossy-gel legacy content icons; two eras on one surface (systematic, so logged as signature-with-cost)

aesthetic.direction: system-native vibrancy utility with a retained skeuomorphic (glossy-gel) accent language — template-default macOS material rather than a committed bespoke direction

psychology: Fitts's Law — oversized ~64pt tiles are large, forgiving drag-drop targets; the interaction is throwing files, so target area is the point
Jakob's Law — reuses the familiar Launchpad grid + system folder icons; instantly legible with zero teaching
Hick's Law / Miller-Cowan chunking — ~15 destinations chunked into 3 labeled sections keeps a dense launcher scannable; a flat grid this size would exceed comfortable choice load
Recognition over recall — every target pairs a familiar icon with a text label (dual coding)
Von Restorff — deliberately NOT exploited: uniform equal-weight grid has no single focal point (correct for a launcher; wrong for a decision surface)
notes: Only two inputs supplied: cover.webp (this UI) and icon.webp — no shot-*.* gallery. Cover is a genuine app screenshot (menu-bar popover over the Sequoia default wallpaper), not a heavy marketing composite; backdrop is just the OS wallpaper, no brand typography to separate. Workflow A only per task, so the app icon (glossy 3D stack of lavender translucent discs with a red hot landing pad on a dark metallic squircle base — Big Sur-era skeuomorphic depth) was read for aesthetic corroboration but NOT given a full icon digest / icons/ file. Era called big-sur not liquid-glass: no lensing evidence, Sequoia wallpaper, glossy content icons; a single translucent still cannot confirm Liquid Glass vs legacy vibrancy. Only one surface (light, no dark-mode, no selected-tile state, no settings) — narrow evidence for a mature multi-window-less app. Single app, no promotions.
